claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was born around AD 185 in Alexandria, Egypt, and died around AD 254 in Tyre, Phoenicia.
The nine homilies on Judges were delivered sometime between AD 238 and AD 248.
Origen composed the homilies to expound Judges 2–7 and to call his audience into a loving relationship with Christ through Scripture.
Origen applied his characteristic allegorical method, interpreting the literal, psychic, and pneumatic senses of the biblical text.
The homilies are significant because they exemplify Origen’s allegorical exegesis and his influence on the practice of lectio divina, a prayerful reading of Scripture praised by Pope Benedict XVI.
